hints: Integrate by parts with u=tan⁻¹x and dv=x dx.
Rewrite x²/(1+x²)=1−1/(1+x²), integrate, and apply 0 and 1 using tan⁻¹1=π/4.
walkthrough:
Set up integration by parts for $\int_0^1 x\tan^{-1}x\,\mathrm{d}x$:
$$u = \tan^{-1}x \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = x \implies v = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$$

Apply the integration by parts formula $\int u\,\mathrm{d}v = uv - \int v\,\mathrm{d}u$:
$$\int x\tan^{-1}x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}x - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{x^2}{1 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Rewrite the integrand $\dfrac{x^2}{1 + x^2}$ by adding and subtracting 1 in the numerator:
$$\dfrac{x^2}{1 + x^2} = \dfrac{(1 + x^2) - 1}{1 + x^2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}$$

Integrate each term:
$$\int \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = x - \tan^{-1}x$$
$$\int x\tan^{-1}x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\tan^{-1}x - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{1}{2}(x^2 + 1)\tan^{-1}x - \dfrac{1}{2}x$$

Evaluate the definite integral using the limits $x = 0$ and $x = 1$:
$$\text{At } x = 1: \quad \dfrac{1}{2}(1^2 + 1)\tan^{-1}(1) - \dfrac{1}{2}(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}(2)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad \dfrac{1}{2}(0 + 1)\tan^{-1}(0) - \dfrac{1}{2}(0) = 0 - 0 = 0$$

Subtract the lower limit value to obtain the final exact value:
$$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}$$
